# What keeps a plant upright?

<!-- STEP id="fixed-in-place" -->
## A plant stays in one place

Most plants are fixed in one place. A neem tree cannot walk to shelter when a storm comes, so its body must stay firm and upright by itself, through rain, wind and its own heavy weight.

<!-- STEP id="the-cell-wall" -->
## The cell wall gives strength

Every plant cell has a **cell wall** outside its cell membrane, as you saw in an earlier chapter, on cells. The wall is stiff, so it gives each cell rigidity and strength.

<!-- STEP id="walls-together" -->
## Many walls make a firm plant

In a stem, thousands of walled cells are packed side by side, and together their walls make the whole stem firm. The stem can bend a little in the wind and still not fall.

**So the answer to the storm question is the cell wall: stiff walls around every cell keep the tree firm and upright.**

image.alt: Two storm scenes. On the left a soft plant has fallen flat, with a red cross. On the right a tree bends in the wind but stays standing, with a green tick. Round close-ups show soft cells and woody tissue.
